hypothesis: If all domestic pigeon breeds descend from Columba livia (with its geographical sub-species) and not from several wild stocks, then every domestic-breed mitochondrial sequence should fall within the Columba livia cluster: nearer to C. livia sequences than to any other Columba species, and within intraspecific distance of C. livia.
pass_criterion: Using GenBank mitochondrial records of Columba livia and of all other Columba species, aligned by best ungapped offset to the COI and CYTB genes of the C. livia reference mitogenome NC_013978: every domestic-labelled sequence (organism 'Columba livia domestica', a /breed qualifier, or a breed name in the record) has its nearest non-domestic sequence in C. livia (or in a wild C. livia subspecies), and the maximum p-distance from any domestic sequence to the nearest C. livia sequence is < 2 %. Requires >= 10 domestic-labelled sequences from >= 5 named breeds or 'domestica' records; otherwise inconclusive (underpowered).
fail_criterion: At least 2 domestic sequences from at least 2 different breeds (or records) are nearer to another Columba species (C. rupestris, C. oenas, C. palumbus, C. guinea, C. leuconota, C. hodgsonii, etc.) than to any C. livia sequence, or exceed 2 % from all C. livia sequences while being within 2 % of another species: refutes (a second wild stock contributes maternal ancestry). Exactly one such sequence: mixed.
interpretation: Darwin's claim concerns descent of all domestic breeds from one wild species; mitochondrial DNA tests the maternal component of that descent, which is what pre-genomic public data allow. 'Columba livia with its geographical sub-species' is taken as all records with organism Columba livia (any subspecies, including domestica for the domestic set). Columba rupestris, the hill pigeon, is a separate species in modern taxonomy and is treated as an alternative wild stock, although Darwin may have regarded it as a form of C. livia; a domestic sequence nearest to C. rupestris is therefore reported separately in the extra fields as well as counted. Alignment is by best ungapped offset because indels are rare in these coding genes; sequences overlapping the reference gene by < 400 bp are discarded.
